topics.name: Getting Started
topics.intro: Where should you begin? Understand when AI helps, choose a first task and check whether your business is ready.

topics.name: Using AI at Work
topics.intro: How can AI help with the work you already do? Explore invoices, reminders and customer follow-up, with practical checks for data and permissions.

topics.name: Tools & Comparisons
topics.intro: Which tool fits the job? Compare options, choose what to try and avoid paying for features you do not need.

topics.name: Costs & Results
topics.intro: Is it worth the time and money? Calculate costs, measure a pilot and decide whether to keep, fix or stop.

articles.imageAlt: Illustration: bank statement lines beside a budget table and a chat prompt.
articles.searchTitle: Turn last month's bank statement into a budget you'll actually keep
articles.searchDek: Holiday spending starts this month. Strip out the personal details, paste in one statement, and get a budget built on how you actually spend.

articles.imageAlt: Illustration: Thanksgiving menu, timeline, and grocery list beside a chat prompt.
articles.searchTitle: Hosting Thanksgiving? One prompt gets you the menu, the timeline and the grocery list
articles.searchDek: Give ChatGPT four facts about your kitchen and ask for a menu, an hour-by-hour plan and one grocery list sorted by aisle. Then check the turkey against USDA.

articles.imageAlt: Illustration: four stylized work roles beside a laptop—documents, numbers, inbox, and office tasks—not product screenshots.
articles.searchTitle: ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini: which one is best at what
articles.searchDek: Our picks, job by job: Claude for long documents, ChatGPT for numbers and images, Gemini or Copilot for everyday office work. Researched, not tested.

articles.imageAlt: Illustration: stack of paper invoices beside a spreadsheet with check and warning icons.
articles.searchTitle: Can AI type your invoices into a spreadsheet?
articles.searchDek: We ran 24 invented invoices, including scans and handwriting, through an AI model and a rules script. AI read messy ones better but missed a bad total.

articles.imageAlt: Illustration: calendar and payment reminders beside a rules flowchart and chat bubble.
articles.searchTitle: AI vs. simple rules for appointment and payment reminders
articles.searchDek: We ran 30 made-up reminder records through a rules script and an AI model three times each. Rules got every routine case right.

articles.imageAlt: Illustration: inbox with inquiry emails and a draft reply under review.
articles.searchTitle: We ran 30 invented customer inquiries through an AI follow-up assistant
articles.searchDek: A 30-case synthetic test: stop checks passed, but one draft made unapproved promises.

articles.imageAlt: Illustration: checklist clipboard beside workflow cards marked pass, caution, and stop.
articles.searchTitle: We tested our AI readiness checklist on 12 made-up workflows
articles.searchDek: We ran our readiness checklist on 12 invented workflows. It's a good brake and a poor compass.

articles.imageAlt: Illustration: lead follow-up timeline from inquiry through handoff to closed deal.
articles.searchTitle: Small-business lead follow-up automation: a blueprint
articles.searchDek: A lifecycle map for capture, handoff, follow-up, and closure, with exceptions and stop conditions to write first.

articles.imageAlt: Illustration: five task cards ranked on an automation scorecard.
articles.searchTitle: 5 tasks your small business should automate before anything else
articles.searchDek: Use a five-question scorecard, simple ROI math, and a worked example to identify repetitive work worth automating.

articles.imageAlt: Illustration: twenty-point readiness scorecard on a workflow diagram.
articles.searchDek: Score one workflow with a 20-point readiness check and turn the result into a one-page pilot brief.

articles.imageAlt: Illustration: side-by-side tool comparison scorecard with pilot checklist.
articles.searchTitle: How to choose your first AI tool without wasting money
articles.searchDek: Compare tools with the same real work, a 35-point scorecard, total-cost math, and a 30-day pilot.

articles.imageAlt: Illustration: decision fork between rules-based automation and AI assistance.
articles.searchTitle: AI vs. automation: when your small business actually needs AI
articles.searchDek: Use the Minimum Intelligence Principle and a four-question decision test to choose between rules, AI, and human judgment.

articles.imageAlt: Illustration: ROI worksheet with savings, costs, and break-even chart.
articles.searchTitle: How to calculate the ROI of AI automation
articles.searchDek: Use a conservative five-number model to calculate net monthly value, break-even volume, and payback period.

articles.imageAlt: Illustration: green, yellow, and red data labels beside documents entering an AI tool.
articles.searchTitle: What data should you put into an AI tool?
articles.searchDek: Use a green-yellow-red data framework and a pre-upload checklist before business information enters an AI workflow.

articles.imageAlt: Illustration: pilot evaluation sheet with keep, fix, and stop columns.
articles.searchTitle: How to evaluate an AI pilot: keep, fix, or stop
articles.searchDek: Use a pilot evidence sheet, quality buckets, net-time math, and a worked example to decide whether an AI workflow deserves to continue.

articles.imageAlt: Illustration: business app icons with permission toggles and an action contract.
articles.searchTitle: AI agents are moving into your business apps
articles.searchDek: Use an Agent Action Contract and a contractor test plan to decide what an assistant may read, draft, propose, and change.
